introduction.en: Money supply in India is measured by the RBI using various aggregates, primarily categorized into Narrow Money (M1) and Broad Money (M3) based on liquidity and components.
introduction.hi: Money supply in India is measured by the RBI using various aggregates, primarily categorized into Narrow Money (M1) and Broad Money (M3) based on liquidity and components.

body.en: Narrow Money (M1) includes currency with the public and demand deposits, representing highly liquid assets used for transactions. Broad Money (M3) includes M1 plus time deposits, reflecting the total credit creation capacity of the banking system. The RBI monitors these to control inflation and growth. By adjusting tools like the Repo Rate and CRR, the RBI influences the money multiplier effect, thereby impacting the growth of M3.
